streamTimeoutDesc: How long a model request may stay silent before we treat it as stuck. Reasoning models (e.g. mimo) can think for minutes without output, but any streaming reasoning still counts as activity. These two knobs control "how long with zero data" and "how long a single turn may run".
streamSaved: Saved — applies to the next request
accentNote: Overrides the current theme's accent instantly across the UI; pick "Default" to restore the theme's own palette.
approvalNoticeDesc: Send a notice after an allowed action completes. L1 high-risk actions still ask before running and send no notice; read-only actions are skipped.
modelTiersDesc: Use a separate model for compaction / decomposition / background workers to cut cost. Leave empty to follow the main model.
approvalSnapshotNote: New chats snapshot the current level; "Always allow" rules are stored on this machine.
autoDecomposeDesc: A lightweight planning pass breaks multi-file/multi-feature tasks into steps you confirm and run one by one; each step reports its cost and lets you decide whether to continue, saving rework tokens when big tasks go off track.
autoDecomposeLabel: Auto-split when a large task is detected
backendNone: No backend available on this platform
computerUseEnable: Allow the Agent to control the UI (Computer Use)
computerUseEnableDesc: When enabled, the Agent can autonomously operate desktop apps (click / type / key / scroll) to finish GUI tasks. Off by default; even when on, every call still prompts an approval card first and sensitive actions ask again step by step.
computerUseNote: UI automation can only be started by the Agent within a session, and every action prompts an approval card first; this page offers no blanket "allow all".
cuaGuideLinuxBody: Linux supports screen capture and vision analysis, but needs one of: scrot / ImageMagick (import) / gnome-screenshot — install one, e.g. apt install scrot. Under a Wayland session capture may be restricted by the compositor. Reading the UI element tree and clicking/typing are macOS-only (they rely on the Accessibility API), so the Agent cannot control the UI on Linux for now.
cuaGuideMacBody:
UI automation requires macOS Accessibility permission; without it the app cannot read UI elements or perform clicks/typing:
1. Click “Open System Settings” below to jump to Privacy & Security › Accessibility
2. Find this app in the list and turn the switch on (if it is listed but was previously disabled, remove it and add it again)
3. Return to this page and click “Recheck” to confirm the status
cuaGuideWinBody: Windows supports screen capture and vision analysis (via built-in PowerShell, no extra install). But reading the UI element tree and clicking/typing still require a Windows UIA implementation, which is not available yet, so the Agent cannot control the UI on Windows for now. The capabilities that do work need no system permission.
cuaNoModels: No models available; add one in model settings first
cuaObjectivePlaceholder: Task objective, e.g. open System Settings and fill the form
cuaRecordIntro: Record: the model completes a task once and saves it as a script. Replay: no model calls; steps are replayed deterministically, and sensitive steps still require per-step confirmation. Recordings stay on this machine only.
cuaRecordNeedFields: Objective and app name are required
cuaReplayAlwaysTitle: Ask for confirmation on every step (not just sensitive ones)
deleteModelFileMsg: Remove "{model}" from "{provider}" in the config file? (written back to models.json)
deleteModelMsg: Remove "{model}" from "{provider}"? The service and its key are unaffected.
deleteProviderFileMsg: This removes "{name}" and its {count} models from the config file (recover by editing models.json manually).
deleteProviderMsg: Delete "{name}"? Its API Key will be destroyed and cannot be recovered.
fileManagedNote: Managed by {path}; removing or adding models here writes back to the config file — edit name and key in the file
githubNote: Once signed in, you can create a Pull Request in one click from the changes panel; creating is an outbound write and prompts an approval card first.
gitMissingHint: git command not detected; install Git first to use the changes panel and worktree features
gitNoUserHint: user.name is not set: commits will fail now. Run git config --global user.name "Your Name" in a terminal
inAppBrowsingDesc: This app embeds no browser engine: web content always opens in the system browser, avoiding a second rendering and cookie stack inside the coding workbench. To fetch page content, use an MCP connector (e.g. fetch / Playwright) through the Agent; results return as text in the conversation.
languageDesc: Interface language. Applies instantly and is remembered.
linkCopyDesc: Never open links; copy to clipboard instead (avoids accidental navigation)
linkOpenNote: Takes effect immediately; applies to link clicks in Markdown previews.
linkSmartDesc: Hand http/https links to the system browser; preview local file paths in-app
linkSystemDesc: Open all links in the system default browser
modelCapsImagesHint: This model understands images: when enabled, dropped screenshots are sent to the model as image content
modelCapsReasoningHint: This model supports reasoning-effort levels (e.g. low / high)
modelCapsToolsHint: This model supports tool calling: when disabled, no tools are sent to it
modelsFileAfter: file once added; saving syncs them into the list below without a restart.
modelsFileBefore: Models are automatically written to the local
modelsFileNotCreated: The file doesn't exist yet; click the path to generate a template.
modelsSynced: Synced {n} model services from the config file
nameAndUrlRequired: Name and base URL are required
newApiKeyPlaceholder: Enter new API Key (stored encrypted on this machine)
noRulesNote: No rules yet. Choosing "Always allow" in an approval prompt adds the tool and scope here, revocable anytime.
noServerModels: No preset models on the server yet
openConfigTitle: Click to open the config file
responseStyleDesc: How detailed the AI's end-of-task summary is. Affects only the wording of the wrap-up, not the work performed.
responseStyleConciseDesc: A one-line conclusion: what was done + what's next, without file lists or process detail.
responseStyleDefaultDesc: A structured wrap-up: what was done, files changed (openable), key decisions, remaining issues and next steps.
responseStyleDetailedDesc: A full report: per-file changes and reasons, verification and results, risks with fixes, and remaining steps — expanded.
sandboxFallbackNote: Command-level hard blocking is enabled as a fallback: dangerous commands (recursive delete, sudo, git push, reset --hard, piped remote scripts, etc.) are rejected outright and cannot be bypassed by approval. This is not OS-level isolation — do not run untrusted code in this environment.
sandboxNotReady: OS-level sandbox not ready on this system ({backend})
searchProvidersDesc: Used by the Agent's web_search tool. Enable several at once: they are tried top to bottom and the first success wins (automatic failover); or enable just one. Once enabled the Agent can search the web with no extra setup.
serverManagedNote: Managed by the server; read-only locally
skillCodeReviewDesc: Review code quality and find potential issues
skillDeepResearchDesc: Native deep-research pipeline: auto-plan subquestions → parallel search → evidence ledger → read key sources → synthesize, producing a report with numbered citations
skillGenDocsDesc: Generate README and comments from code
skillGenTestsDesc: Generate unit test cases for functions
skillGitCommitDesc: Generate well-formed commit messages from changes
skillLatexCompileDesc: Detect Tectonic/TeX Live toolchains and compile LaTeX projects; PDF output opens in the preview pane
skillLatexDoctorDesc: Probe TeX engines one by one and report availability with actionable install guidance
switchToAutoMessage: In this mode all tool calls (including file writes and command execution) run automatically without confirmation prompts. Are you sure?
themePreviewNote: Hover a card to preview it live across the UI; the top-bar palette icon and ⌘K "Switch Theme" allow quick switching.
updateNote: Auto-update works only in packaged releases (requires a publish repo in the build config)
urlMustBeHttp: Base URL must be a full URL starting with http:// or https://
writeBoundaryDesc: This page is read-only: it never edits global git config or signs you in. Make config changes explicitly in a terminal so settings can't become a backdoor for silently mutating your environment.
writeBoundaryNote: In-session git writes (commit / checkout / restore) go through the approval center, configured on the General page; the Diff panel's "undo" relies on local disk snapshots, not git state.
switchToFullAccessMessage: The full-access tier disables the OS sandbox, the write allow-list and protected-path guards; agent commands will run with your full user permissions. Continue?
memoryNeedProject: Open a project to view and manage its memories here.
memoryAutoCaptureDesc: When on, each finished turn stores a "question → conclusion" summary into project memory (model-conclusion trust tier); off by default — use the /mem command to save explicitly.
memoryTeamAutoDesc: When a sub-task completes, its conclusion is stored as team memory (visible to this team only, capped at 200 entries). Independent from session auto-capture above: on by default; turning it off does not affect conversation memory, and vice versa.
memoryUnavailable: Memory service unavailable (local database not ready)
memoryListEmpty: No memories for this project yet
memoryDeleteMsg: It will no longer be injected into future conversations. This cannot be undone.
memoryTeamSharingDesc: When enabled, the project memory file (.mjcode/memory.md) is no longer ignored by .gitignore, so it can be committed and shared with your team.
memoryResetScopeHint: Clear all memories in a layer (irreversible).
memoryResetScopeMsg: All memories in this layer will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
memoryPromotionHint: Team memories with frequent hits can be promoted to project memory after your confirmation; nothing is written automatically, to avoid team-specific conventions polluting cross-team context.
mcpCrashHint: The server process exited unexpectedly; its tools are unusable. Reconnecting automatically with backoff; if it never recovers, click Reconnect to retry manually.
employeeIdHint: File name on disk: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only.
employeeIdInvalid: Identifier may contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only
employeePromptPh: Describe this employee's role, responsibilities and working style.
employeePromptHint: Up to {max} characters. Injection scanning runs on save; flagged prompts are not injected into context.
employeeToolsHint: Leave empty to inherit all built-in tools.
employeeDeleteMsg: '{name}' cannot be restored, and existing sessions lose this role preset.
employeeBridgeMissing: This build's main process does not expose the employee write channel (ecosystem:employeeCreate) yet, so saving is unavailable.
employeeAiPlaceholder: Describe the digital employee you want in one sentence (e.g. an expert who reviews frontend performance)
employeeAiHint: The draft fills in the name, id, role prompt and tools below automatically; you can still edit them before saving.
hooksDesc: Run your own scripts before and after tool calls. preToolUse can block: a non-zero exit code rejects that tool call; you can also print {"decision":"deny","reason":"..."} to stdout. postToolUse is observation only (audit/notify) and never rewrites tool results. If the script is missing, times out, or fails to start, the tool call is allowed — hooks never block the task.
hooksStdinHint: The script receives one JSON line on stdin: { event, tool, channel, args, cwd, conversationId, result? } (result only for postToolUse).
winSandboxDesc: Run commands as a restricted dedicated user with outbound network blocked (mirrors Codex's Windows approach). Until the one-time administrator setup is done, commands fall back to command-level hard blocking.
winSandboxReadyLabel: Ready: commands run as the restricted dedicated user
winSandboxNotReadyLabel: Not ready: one-time administrator setup required
winSandboxUacNote: Running the setup triggers UAC and writes to the system (creates dedicated users, sets ACLs, adds firewall rules); any failed step rolls back automatically. The password is randomly generated and stored locally encrypted via DPAPI, never in plaintext.
winSandboxPlanTitle: Commands to run (the plaintext password appears as a placeholder)
winSandboxSetupConfirmMessage: This triggers UAC and creates dedicated users, sets workspace ACLs, and adds a firewall outbound-block rule as administrator. Any failed step rolls back automatically. Continue?
winSandboxTeardownConfirmMessage: This deletes the dedicated users and firewall rule, and clears the locally stored encrypted credential. Continue?
